items.name: Combat
items.desc: Designed to protect soldiers in any situation, Combat Armor gives the wearer equal amounts of resistance to physical and energy damage.

items.name: Excavator Power Armour
items.desc: Developed by Garrahan Mining Co., the "Excavator" class of Power Armor never saw full production, despite being heavily advertised in Appalachia as the future of mining.

items.name: Leather
items.desc: Thick layers of animal hide makes Leather Armor particularly suited to protecting against energy damage.

items.name: Marine
items.desc: Outclassed only by Power Armor, every piece of Marine Combat Armor provides exceptional protection in nearly every battlefield scenario.

items.name: Metal
items.desc: Constructed of thick, hand-welded steel or aluminum, Metal Armor offers additional protection against physical damage.

items.name: Power Armor Raider
items.desc: Scavenged and restored by Appalachia's vicious and anarchistic gangs, Raider Power Armor features crude plating, rusty spikes, and significant battlefield protection.

items.name: Power Armour Frame
items.desc: Even without additional limb armor, a Power Armor frame still provides tactical advantages, like increased carry weight, greater melee damage and the elimination of falling damage.

items.name: Robot
items.desc: Crafted from actual destroyed robots, the high-tech plating of Robot Armor offers additional protection against energy damage.

items.name: T-45 Power Armour
items.desc: Built by defense contractor West Tek, the T-45 series of Power Armor was the first to be successfully deployed on the battlefield. Its introduction changed the nature of modern warfare.

items.name: T-51 Power Armour
items.desc: The Battle of Anchorage saw the first deployment of the advanced T-51 series of Power Armor. With advanced servos and composite armor plating, it was a vast improvement over earlier models.

items.name: T-60 Power Armour
items.desc: The most advanced suits of Power Armor to see extensive use were the T-60 models. By the time of the Great War, they were a common sight in all U.S. military engagements.

items.name: Underarmor
items.desc: If you're worried your Vault Suit doesn't offer enough protection, you can mix and match pieces of all armor types and wear them directly over it.

items.name: Addictol
items.desc: Addictol completely cures its user of all addictions.

items.name: Buffout
items.desc: A powerful steroid, Buffout grants temporary bonuses to Strength, Endurance, and maximum Health.

items.name: Calmex
items.desc: Highly sought after by hunters and assassins throughout the Wasteland, Calmex grants a temporary bonus to Perception, Agility, and Sneak Attack damage.

items.name: Daddy O
items.desc: Who needs friends when you're this smart? Using Daddy-O grants a temporary bonus to Intelligence and Perception, but also a temporary penalty to Charisma.

items.name: Daytripper
items.desc: Sold as "happiness in a bottle," Daytripper grants a temporary bonus to Charisma and Luck, but also a temporary penalty to Strength.

items.name: Med X
items.desc: A powerful painkiller, Med-X grants a temporary bonus to Damage Resistance.

items.name: Mentats
items.desc: Popular with students and scientists alike, Mentats grant a temporary bonus to Perception and Intelligence.

items.name: Psycho
items.desc: Developed by the United States military as a combat drug, Psycho grants a temporary bonus to Damage dealt and Damage Resistance.

items.name: Rads
items.desc: To fight radiation, use the chems Rad-X and RadAway. Take Rad-X to temporarily increase your Radiation Resistance. Take RadAway if you've already been exposed.

items.name: Stimpak
items.desc: The medication inside a Stimpak heals injuries and can even restore damaged limbs.

items.name: Xcell
items.desc: The experimental chem X-Cell grants a temporary bonus to every SPECIAL attribute.

items.name: Assaultron
items.desc: The RobCo Assaultron is a frontline combat robot with exceptional melee capabilities. But it is her powerful head-mounted laser that, once fully charged, can decimate an enemy.

items.name: Cargobot
items.desc: Late in 2060, the U.S. military deployed their unmanned Cargobots all over Appalachia. They proved ideal for providing reconnaissance and delivering supplies in even the most hostile conditions.

items.name: Deathclaw
items.desc: Razor-sharp claws, towering size, and surprising speed have made the Deathclaw one of the most feared predators of the Wasteland.

items.name: Feral Ghoul
items.desc: Feral Ghouls were once human beings. Their minds are completely gone, destroyed by radiation, leading only to violent, uncontrollable rage.

items.name: Flatwoods Monster
items.desc: In pre-war West Virginia, near the town of Flatwoods, many claimed to see a dark, mysterious figure with glowing eyes. Was this Flatwoods Monster some kind of demon? Or something far worse?

items.name: Grafton Monster
items.desc: The source of endless fireside horror stories, the Grafton Monster is said to be a lumbering, pale, headless horror that wanders the woodlands of Grafton, West Virginia.

items.name: Honey Beast
items.desc: The Honey Beast is a horribly mutated honey bee that can attack by releasing dangerous insect swarms. Fortunately, it is particularly vulnerable to both heat and cold attacks.

items.name: Liberator
items.desc: The Liberator robot was deployed by air onto American soil in the days leading up to the Great War. Its purpose was to inspire invading Chinese troops and spread Communist propaganda.

items.name: Mega Sloth
items.desc: The enormous Mega Sloth is peaceful by nature, but highly protective of its territory. It's also not nearly as slow as one might expect.

items.name: Mirelurk
items.desc: While there are actually several Mirelurk species, most are heavily armored and aggressive. If facing one in combat, try to aim for an unprotected area, like the face.

items.name: Miss Nanny
items.desc: General Atomics International built the Miss Nanny robot as a female counterpart to the Mister Handy. Both are equally adept in their duties and feature the same interchangeable implements.

items.name: Mister Farmhand
items.desc: The Vault-Tec Agricultural Research Center promised a future of automated, high-tech farming. But sometime after the war, their experimental Mister Farmhands turned that dream into a nightmare.

items.name: Mister Gutsy
items.desc: Realizing their robots' enormous military potential, General Atomics International developed the Mister Gutsy as a powerful wartime equivalent to the Mister Handy.

items.name: Mister Handy
items.desc: The pride of General Atomics International, the Mister Handy was designed as the ultimate domestic servant. If needed, however, his various attachments can be used for defense.

items.name: Mole Miner
items.desc: Trapped within their deteriorating mining suits, the Mole Miners are frenzied combatants who attack anything they perceive as a threat.

items.name: Mole Rat
items.desc: While vulnerable out in the open, Mole Rats can burrow underground in seconds. This allows them to set up ambushes or escape from predators with alarming speed.

items.name: Mothman
items.desc: According to local folklore - as well as a statue and museum in Point Pleasant, West Virginia - the Mothman is a terrifying half-man, half-moth hybrid. Pray you never encounter it and learn the truth.

items.name: Mutant Hound
items.desc: Mutant Hounds are typically raised and trained by Super Mutants, who use them as vicious guard and attack dogs.

items.name: Protectron
items.desc: While RobCo's Protectron robots were meant to replace human workers in areas that were deemed too dangerous, many people in Appalachia actually saw them as a threat to their jobs.

items.name: Rad Stag
items.desc: Radstags have a natural fear of predators and are likely to run as soon as they see you. If cornered, they can employ their sharp hooves to surprisingly deadly effect.

items.name: Radscorpion
items.desc: While the venom of their stingers is deadly, the real threat from a Radscorpion is their ability to ambush their prey from underground.

items.name: Radtoad
items.desc: Radtoads use their elongated tongues to ambush prey at a distance. If attacked, they unleash clouds of poison gas and send out swarms of their own offspring to harass opponents.

items.name: Scorched
items.desc: The Scorched are human beings afflicted by a strange condition known as the Scorched Plague, and are now controlled by a violent hive mind. But what is the Plague's source? And can it be stopped?

items.name: Sentry Bot
items.desc: The Sentry Bot was designed for one purpose: security through overwhelming firepower. Its only real weakness is the short "cool down" phase after attacking, when its Fusion Core is most vulnerable.

items.name: Snallygaster
items.desc: A horrifying result of experiments with the experimental Forced Evolutionary Virus, the Snallygaster has six legs, numerous eyes along its back, and an extended tongue covered in acidic goo.

items.name: Stingwing
items.desc: Stingwings use their impressive speed and poisoned stingers to wear down their opponents, but a well-placed hit or two can easily shatter their frail bodies.

items.name: Super Mutant
items.desc: The first Super Mutants in Appalachia were created right before the Great War, when West Tek poisoned the drinking water of Huntersville with the FEV Virus, in a sinister, secret experiment gone horribly wrong.

items.name: Tick
items.desc: What's worse than walking through the forest and getting munched on by a Tick? Walking through post-apocalyptic Appalachia and getting munched on by a giant, mutated, irradiated Tick.

items.name: Wendigo
items.desc: Few creatures, real or imagined, terrify West Virginians quite like the Wendigo. Possessing alarming speed, razor-sharp claws and an insatiable hunger for raw flesh, it is truly the stuff of nightmares.
To guarantee a fair fight, Nuclear Winter strips you of everything but your cosmetics. Your belongings are returned at the end of a match.
In Nuclear Winter you take less damage from falling from heights and can fall from higher distances.
Your SPECIAL provides no bonuses in Nuclear Winter, and only affects how many Nuclear Winter Perk Cards of a certain stat you can equip.
Caps and XP earned in Nuclear Winter are awarded at the end of a match based on your performance!
Stimpaks in Nuclear Winter stop healing when you take damage. Find a safe place before using them!
You can earn Perk Cards for use in Nuclear Winter by playing matches!
Hunger and Thirst aren't a factor in Nuclear Winter. Focus on surviving the fight!
We've suppressed your diseases and the ability to contract diseases for the time being. Fight your enemies, not viruses!
You can only equip seven total Perk Cards in Nuclear Winter.
Nuclear Winter uses its own exclusive Perk Cards, including many you cannot find anywhere else!
Spending time in the storm can be a new and exciting experience that is also extremely detrimental to your health!
There's no time for addiction! While in Nuclear Winter, take all the chems you need without the fear for any nasty repercussions.
Use your C.A.M.P. Kits freely since you can't take them with you. They don't grow on trees, but they might be made of them!
We've suppressed whatever mutations you might have come in with, but that won't stop you from temporarily contracting new ones!
Don't worry about finding bobby pins. A Nuclear Winter Picklock Perk is all you need!
Hacking a Nuclear Winter terminal can unlock some great loot and even display the position of enemies on your map!
You can revive teammates without using a Stimpak in Nuclear Winter, but it takes longer than usual.
The crossbow can hold up to 3 bolts at once!
ZAX has replaced items in most containers with more useful items. Search every nook and cranny!
Cosmetics from the Atomic Shop can be brought into Nuclear Winter! Find the item you want to bring in and select "NW Favorite" and you'll bring them to your next match!

items.name: Ghoul Blackout Quest
items.desc: Your new life as a ghoul begins...

items.name: Perk Penetrator
items.desc: There's nowhere to hide! When in V.A.T.S., the Penetrator Perk allows you to target an enemy's body parts that are blocked by cover.

items.name: Pv E
items.desc: Quickplay PvE matches you with other players, ready to face the challenges of Appalachia as a team.

items.name: Pv E
items.desc: Each Quickplay PvE session features an Event that you and your team are tasked with completing. Work together!

items.name: Pv E
items.desc: Already grouped up with your friends? Quickplay PvE will match you all together.

items.name: Pv E SFZ08
items.desc: You and your team are entering the Irrational Fear event. Help a struggling Mr. Handy unit retrieve honey. What could go wrong?

items.name: Team Deathmatch
items.desc: Eliminate enemy players to score points and bring victory for your side in Team Deathmatch!

items.name: Team Deathmatch
items.desc: The arenas for Team Deathmatch are randomly picked from one of the many locations within Appalachia.

items.name: Team Deathmatch
items.desc: Team Deathmatch is timed. The highest scoring team within the time limit, or the first team to score 50 points, wins.

items.name: TWZ09
items.desc: The bleach dogwoods need fertilizer to prevent them from dying off.

items.name: Vault V94 Mission01
items.desc: Mirelurks and Feral Ghouls are just as deadly in deep water as they are on dry land. Someone in a full suit of Power Armor... is not.

items.name: Vault V94 Mission01
items.desc: Strangler Hearts are most vulnerable when their deadly blooms open to attack.

items.name: Vault V94 Mission02
items.desc: Relying on Chems to survive in highly irradiated areas can be dangerous... and expensive. Choose the right Perks and gear to help manage your Rads.

items.name: Vault V94 Mission02
items.desc: Splitting up can be an effective way to search multiple areas quickly. Just make sure each group brings enough firepower.

items.name: Vault V94 Mission03
items.desc: Vault-Tec Seed Banks are organized by genus and species. Consult a Seed Bank Management Terminal for details.

items.name: Vault V94 Mission03
items.desc: Shutting down the Flood Control Pumps will significantly delay the Emergency Flooding Procedure.

items.name: 76Exit Event Quest
items.desc: Feral Ghouls are lurking just outside Vault 76! Drive them back.

items.name: A Colossal Problem
items.lsst: A Colossal Problem  Find out what lurks at the bottom of Monongah Mine.  - Kill Wendigo Spawns quickly; they will stagger you  - Falling embers warn you of a dangerous hazard  - The mine is unstable; beware of it collapsing

items.name: A rowdy Eyebot called JES-2R is leading a crew of mischief-makers to wreak havoc on the Whitespring Resort.
items.lsst: A rowdy Eyebot called JES-2R is leading a crew of mischief-makers to wreak havoc on the Whitespring Resort.  - Sow mayhem by taking part in various destructive activities  - Be prepared for Whitespring Security to fight back  - Wear a costume to gain bonus progress and unique rewards!

items.name: A rowdy Eyebot called JES-2R is leading a crew of mischief-makers to wreak havoc through Rapidan Camp.
items.lsst: A rowdy Eyebot called JES-2R is leading a crew of mischief-makers to wreak havoc through Rapidan Camp.  - Sow mayhem by taking part in various destructive activities  - Be prepared for enemies to fight back

items.name: Beasts of Burden
items.desc: Vinny's nephew Luca has managed to land himself in a tricky situation.
items.lsst: Beasts of Burden  Help Luca recover stolen goods after a deal gone wrong! Load up the Brahmin with cargo and get ready to fend off cultists... and anything else that might be lurking in the fog.  - Gather Luca's homemade explosives from the cultist camp  - Grab cargo and load up as much as you can

items.name: Blast
items.desc: MODUS has tasked you with luring "pests" into the range of an orbital strike.

items.name: Blue Ridge Caravan
items.desc: Guide the Blue Ridge Caravan Co. through the Big Bend Tunnel.

items.name: Bo SZ03
items.desc: The artillery at Fort Defiance is operational and ready to deal a blow to the Scorched. All it needs is a target.

items.name: Campfire Tales
items.lsst: Campfire Tales  Scout Leader Penny has some scary stories to tell around the campfire. Be careful, as some stories are more real than others.   - Follow Penny's instructions as the objectives update  - Perform the requested tasks  - Keep gathering twigs and don't let the campfire burn out

items.name: CB02 Monster Mash
items.desc: The Monster Mash is happening at Watoga High School! Get candy and turn it in for fabulous prizes. To collect candy, wear the paper mache pinata mask, or attack the person who is!

items.name: CB06 ASAM
items.desc: Defend the Automated Surface-To-Air Missile (ASAM) turret so it can strike at the Scorchbeasts!

items.name: CBZ09 Census
items.desc: A Census Taker robot wants you to "correct" some of his numbers... with murder.

items.name: CBZ13 Robots
items.desc: An automated military convoy is under attack by sabotaged robots! Fight back the waves of robots to secure the convoy.

items.name: Dangerous Pastimes
items.lsst: Dangerous Pastimes  Some settlers require help with their thrill-seeking activities.  -Find and collect parts to repair the Lightning Harvesters  -Charge the Lightning Harvesters by killing Charged enemies  -Defeat the Charged Boss within the time limit

items.name: Distinguished Guests
items.lsst: Distinguished Guests  Mister Billingsley is setting up for a Halloween gala and he could use your help getting everything ready. After all, the key to any great shindig is preparation.  - Find the missing waiter bots by checking both the golf course and clubhouse  - Collect plates and floral centerpieces to set the tables  - Prevent undesirable guests from ruining the party preparations  - Get everything ready before the timer expires

items.name: Encryptid
items.lsst: Encryptid  A rogue creature is terrorizing Appalachia; could it be the fabled Sheepsquatch?  - Recall the creature by using an Assaultron Recall Keycard at the terminal  - The creature will not take damage while in Stealth Mode  - Watch your health, as you will take damage as a conduit  - Avoid entering or standing in the burning areas created by the creature  - Defeat the creature before the conduits run out of power

items.name: ENz01 Above
items.desc: The Kovac-Muldoon is ready to drop a cache of resources. You will need to calibrate its satellite positioning so it can find you.

items.name: ENz04 Bots
items.desc: MODUS has tasked you with helping him create an automated robot patrol force.

items.name: Eviction Notice
items.lsst: Eviction Notice  A Foundation Outpost has been attacked by Super Mutants and is broadcasting a call for help.   -Find and protect the rad scrubber  -Destroy the meat bags  -Be prepared for a Super Mutant onslaught

items.name: Fasnacht Day
items.lsst: Fasnacht Day  The robots have decided it's time to celebrate Fasnacht in Helvetia again. Join the fun during the Fasnacht Day parade and earn a chance at a festival mask!  - Find the Protectron marchers and help them with their tasks so they can join the parade  - Protect the parade marchers, as your reward depends on how many survive  - Light the bonfire to end the celebration

items.name: Feed the People
items.lsst: Feed the People  Use the machinery at Mama Dolce's Food Processing to create cans of nutritious stew. There's nothing like a hot meal from a can on an irradiated day!  - Collect the ingredients scattered around the processing plant and place them into the hopper  - Protect the machinery  - Repair the machinery when it becomes inoperable

items.name: FF01 Death Blossoms
items.desc: Corpse Flowers are in bloom! They're valuable for crafting, but their scent attracts all kinds of creatures, most of them hostile...

items.name: FF08 Project Beanstalk
items.desc: Pharmabot JD-7E has been tasked with using an experimental chemical to improve crop yields. Defend him as he goes about his duties.

items.name: FF09 Reaper
items.desc: The Farmhand Supervisor bots are targeting civilians! Deal with them and reprogram the Mister Farmhands.

items.name: FF11 Raid
items.desc: A Cargo Drop is incoming! Clear out the Scorched or the drop will be canceled.

items.name: FF12 Bell
items.desc: The church bells are causing the Mole Rats in the area to go on a digging frenzy!

items.name: FFZ11 Pack
items.desc: This forest is overrun with packs of wolves. Fight them off and bring down the pack Alpha!

items.name: FFZ16 Swatter
items.desc: A Vertibot is flying over the area. Shoot it down and claim valuable scrap!

items.name: Free Range
items.lsst: Free Range  A pack of Brahmin lost their robotic handler on the way back to the farm. Guide them home, and watch out for wild Sheepsquatch!  - Loot and equip a Shepherd's Crook so you can urge the Brahmin to move faster  - Protect the Brahmin from the dangers on the road, as your reward depends on how many survive  - If the Brahmin split up, you should too

items.name: FSS01 Trap
items.desc: Lure a Scorchbeast into a trap and finish it off!

items.name: Gearin' Up
items.lsst: Gearin' Up  Gather materials to help train a Deathclaw.  - Collect scrap for the armor sets  - Help to train the Deathclaw by fighting alongside it  - Engage in battle against a much stronger foe

items.name: Grahm's Meat Cook
items.lsst: Grahm's Meat Cook  There's nothing like a summer BBQ. Grahm hasn't hosted a party in a long time, so he needs your help.  - Clean up the messes to keep things clean and healthy  - Help entertain with musical instruments  - Donate Prime Meat, Greens, Critter Chunks, and Chally's Feed to the party  - Help turn the spits and put out accidental fires

items.name: Guided Meditation
items.lsst: Guided Meditation  Join a "Guided Meditation" and find inner peace. Do battle with the discordant forces around you and achieve harmony.  - Light the Brazier of Transcendence to begin the meditation  - Spread out to defend the Meditation Hubs located around the temple  - Repair the Meditation Hubs if they are damaged

items.name: Heart of the Swamp
items.lsst: Heart of the Swamp  Strangler vines are infesting the plants and creatures in this area, giving birth to a deadly Strangler Heart. It seems the apocalypse will involve a bit of extreme gardening.  - Destroy the Strangler Heart and the creatures that defend it  - The Strangler Heart cannot be damaged when it is closed

items.name: Horde
items.desc: Hostile creatures are infesting the region! Eliminate the Alpha to stop the Horde from growing.

items.name: Hordes
items.desc: Creatures will sometimes band together in a Horde, led by a powerful Alpha creature. Defeat the Alpha to stop the Horde from spawning more creatures.

items.name: Invaders from beyond have touched down in Appalachia, and are using brainwave siphons to forcibly extract data from nearby lifeforms.
items.lsst: Invaders from beyond have touched down in Appalachia, and are using brainwave siphons to forcibly extract data from nearby lifeforms.  - Draw out and defeat alien commanders to bring down the force fields on the brainwave siphons  - Keep your ears open for deadly energy pulses from the brainwave siphons  - As the attack progresses, watch out for missile strikes from the overhead UFO

items.name: Jailbreak
items.lsst: Jailbreak  There's been a jail break! Help the Warden bring the escaped prisoners to justice and don't let Mad Dog Malone escape.  - Defeat the escaped prisoners  - Repair turrets for extra firepower

items.name: Line in the Sand
items.lsst: Line in the Sand  The automated defenses at Fort Defiance can drive off the Scorched, but you'll need to repair them first. Those Scorched will never know what hit them!  - Repair the defenses  - Protect the Sonic Generator

items.name: Lode Baring
items.lsst: Lode Baring  A mine rich with resources has opened up - but not for long. Grab as much as you can before the mine collapses.  - Repair and protect the Auto-Miners so they can prospect ore  - Seismic activity may uncover hidden troves containing bonus treasures  - Redeem your Claim Tokens at the Exchange Terminal once you're topside again

items.name: Moonshine Jamboree
items.lsst: Moonshine Jamboree  Moonshiner Ned is throwing a jamboree to make a special batch of moonshine.  -Light the fire to get the jamboree started  -Defend the stills from the attacking creatures  -Kill Acidic Gulpers and deliver their venom to the tub

items.name: Most Wanted
items.lsst: Most Wanted  It's bandito o'clock at the Wild West Showdown! Head on over to the town for some rootin', tootin', shootin' and lootin'!   - Loot the townsfolk and safes for Buckaroos  - Deposit the loot in the Getaway Wagon before the time runs out    - After looting, you'll need to defend the wagon at high noon to win the game

items.name: MTR05 Mother Breach
items.desc: Treasure from the depths! Secure the area and take the largest haul you can muster.

items.name: MTR10 Battle
items.desc: Security bots are safeguarding something in this area. Engage them and find out what it is!

items.name: Neurological Warfare
items.desc: The Hawksbill Weather Station is on high alert and needs a Vault-Tec representative to de-escalate the situation.
items.lsst: Neurological Warfare  A nuke made the Hawksbill Weather Station send out an alert broadcast stating it was going to deploy defenses. You should go help de-escalate the alert.  -Investigate the Hawksbill Weather Station to de-escalate the alert  -Defeat the Storm Goliath defenses which grow stronger after each one is destroyed  -The Storm Goliaths will call down lightning to destroy floor panels, exposing hazardous terrain  -Be wary of faulty laser barriers - they will turn on and off at random

items.name: One Violent Night
items.lsst: One Violent Night  A strange creature attacks Buck's Den Beer House whenever it hears the sounds of partying. The louder the racket, the faster the creature will show up to object.  - Play instruments, swing instrument weapons, and keep the jukebox rocking  - Swinging instrument weapons while under the influence of alcohol attracts the creature faster  - Defeat the creature when it shows up and make the beer house a safe place to party again

items.name: Path to Enlightenment
items.lsst: Path to Enlightenment  A local cult believed it could commune with the Mothman. Complete their ritual and see if this legendary creature will reveal itself!  - Collect Bioluminescent Fluid from Fireflies to light the lamp and attract the Mothman  - Kill the Radtoads that eat the Fireflies to gain Bioluminescent Fluid  - Light the lamp at the top of the lighthouse by depositing the Fluid

items.name: Power Plant Event
items.desc: Repair all the systems in the power plant to get it back online.

items.name: Primal Cuts
items.lsst: Primal Cuts  Grahm is hosting a BBQ and needs some really good meat to cook up for his friends. This is your chance to help out. Don't forget to use your Primal Meat at Grahm's Meat Cook!  - Beat the steel drum to attract Prime Beasts  - Kill Prime Beasts as quickly as you can to finish the waves before the timer expires  - Defeat every wave of enemies to earn Prime Meat

items.name: Project Paradise
items.lsst: Project Paradise  Take part in a long lost experiment in the Arktos Pharma Biome Lab, and you may make some unexpected new friends.  - Collect the preferred food in each habitat and deposit it into the feeder  - The more food supplied, the tougher the creature it will attract  - Protect the friendly creatures from predators, as the number of survivors determines your reward

items.name: Radiation Rumble
items.lsst: Radiation Rumble  Scavengers in Emmett Mountain Disposal Site are excavating valuable minerals. Help them out, but be prepared for heavy radiation!  - Keep the scavenging team alive to complete the mission  - Collect irradiated ore from the tunnels below the scavengers' base  - Heavy radiation zones can be lethal, even with high rad resistance  - Remove radiation with the nearby decontamination arches  - The site is infested with ghouls, but be prepared for other surprises as well

items.name: RE Scene MTNZ05 Messenger
items.desc: A Mister Messenger needs your help while he makes a delivery.

items.name: RS02 Beat
items.desc: Steelheart is once again ready to protect Morgantown. Escort him on his patrol.

items.name: Safe and Sound
items.desc: Vera needs help with a pest control problem at the Blue Ridge Middle Mountain Pitstop.
items.lsst: Safe and Sound  The repeller speakers are on the fritz and critters have overrun the Blue Ridge Middle Mountain Pitstop. Vera needs your help recovering the Pitstop and getting the speakers running again.  - Clear out the critters that have overrun the Pitstop  - Repair their experimental repeller speaker system around the Pitstop  - Protect the Pitstop from any more unwanted guests

items.name: Scorched Earth
items.lsst: Scorched Earth  A Scorchbeast Queen and her army of mind-controlled minions are terrorizing the area. Stop them if you can! Make sure you are prepared and wear protection in the blast area.  - Avoid falling into trenches while looking upwards at the flying enemies  - Find cover and avoid being hit by the sonic attack  - Don't fall into the fissure, as it instantly melts flesh

items.name: Seismic Activity
items.desc: The Rollercoaster is currently under maintenance, for your own safety please keep the area clear.
items.lsst: Seismic Activity  Some unexplained discoveries weigh heavy on the Traveling Nuka Carnival folk.   - Destroy the glowing crystals around the coaster using melee attacks   - The crystals seem to have strange properties; who knows what it does to the local wildlife?   - The ground around the coaster is unstable; be careful of earthquakes   - Always be prepared for the worst in these situations

items.name: SFZ08 Fear
items.desc: Beckham the Mister Handy is programmed to retrieve honey. Unfortunately, he's also programmed to be irrationally afraid of bees...

items.name: Sinkhole Solutions
items.lsst: Sinkhole Solutions  Help Willow clear out dangerous creatures in a deadly sandstorm!  - Activate the Stomper to draw out the Radscorpions  - Kill the Radscorpions and destroy their nests  - Engage in a final battle to clear all the pests from the sinkholes

items.name: Spin the Wheel
items.desc: SPIN THE WHEEL   Come one, come all, to Cappy and Bottle's spectacular Nuka World On Tour game show!
items.lsst: Spin the Wheel  Join Cappy and Bottle in their exciting attraction exclusive to Nuka World on Tour. Step onto the stage, spin the wheel and discover what thrills await you; no two games are ever the same!  - Spin the wheel to see your challenge  - Participate in five unique rounds  - Claim a prize based on your performance!

items.name: Supply Drop
items.desc: Want to start an event that will summon a Cargobot to drop off supplies? Load a US Government Supply Requisition holotape into an Emergency Broadcast Terminal.

items.name: Swarm of Suitors
items.lsst: Swarm of Suitors  Mirelurks are gathering for a mating ritual. Stop them from reaching their spawning grounds and keep an eye out for the Mirelurk Queen!  - Make sure someone is standing on the island  - Prevent the Mirelurks from reaching the island and destroy the would-be suitors

items.name: Tea Time
items.lsst: Tea Time  The Giant Teapot is ready to brew! Defend it while it boils up a fresh pot. It's a lot of work for a cup of tea, but it's the civilized thing to do.  - Start up the boilers by activating them from within the teapot  - Protect the water pipes located behind the service station, behind the teapot, and under the water tower  - Watch out for sneaky little bugs that hate the vibration of the brewing system

items.name: Test Your Metal
items.lsst: Test Your Metal  A Brotherhood of Steel team is investigating Rust Eagle combat bots. Help them survive the arena so they can report their findings!  - Keep the Brotherhood gladiators alive  - Revive gladiators that have been downed  - Defeat 3 rounds of Rust Eagle robots to emerge victorious

items.name: The Big Bloom
items.lsst: The Big Bloom  Pick flowers for the elderly in a blossoming minefield.  - Collect wild flowers growing around Black-Eyed Susan's cabin. Watch out for mines!  - Destroy invading Overgrown  - Eliminate Beezlebub, the Giant Bee of Yore

items.name: The Mothman Equinox
items.lsst: The Mothman Equinox  Join the Wise Mothman's Enlightened in performing a summoning ritual.  - Look to the rooftops for Totems of Warding  - Blood troughs can be found on the streets. Look for orange banners  - Be sure to protect all of the pyres. Enemy waves will not relent  - Don't forget to return to the museum rooftop before the Wise One arrives

items.name: Tunnel of Love
items.lsst: Tunnel of Love  The Tunnel of Love is out of commission! Enter the old mineshaft and help Mr. Lovely fix up the attraction.  - Finish setting up the heart lamps  - Repair the broken tracks  - Find some discarded parts and build Mr. Lovely a partner to share the ride with

items.name: TW003
items.desc: Mad Dog Malone is on the loose again! Bring him to justice.

items.name: TW006
items.desc: Grafton's mayor has tasked you with putting down a group of "protestors."

items.name: TW009
items.desc: A Civil War Reenactment is being held at Prickett's Fort, and you're invited to join in the battle!

items.name: TW043
items.desc: The Warden has asked you to help his officers with their rounds.

items.name: TWZ07
items.desc: The Mayor of Grafton is holding a town parade!

items.name: Uranium Fever
items.lsst: Uranium Fever  Defend the Uranium Extractors and collect whatever valuables they pull up. The more uranium that is collected, the greater the reward.  - Protect the Uranium Extractors from the Mole Miners  - Repair the Uranium Extractors whenever they are too damaged to continue extracting

items.name: Vigilant
items.desc: Rover the robot needs to repair the communications uplink. Protect him until his work is complete.

items.name: Workshop Attack
items.desc: This Workshop is under attack! Prepare defenses and drive back enemies to keep it operational.

items.name: Workshop Attack Scorchbeasts
items.desc: A Scorchbeast is attacking! Prepare defenses and drive it back to keep the Workshop operational.

items.name: Workshop Attack Takeover
items.desc: This Workshop has been overrun! Take it back!

items.name: Workshops
items.desc: Workshops are areas that produce valuable resources. When claimed, you can build resource collectors and defenses to protect them from both dangerous creatures and hostile players.

items.name: Bo S02
items.desc: Taggerdy's Thunder was a US Army Ranger unit led by Lieutenant Elizabeth Taggerdy. She continued to lead her troops - as a Paladin - after they all joined the Brotherhood of Steel.

items.name: Bo S04
items.desc: Paladin Taggerdy was known for only recruiting from those who had military experience and found it difficult to coordinate with the other, more "civilian" factions in Appalachia.

items.name: Bo S05
items.desc: Built from the ruins of Allegheny Asylum, Fort Defiance served as headquarters for the newly-established Appalachian branch of the Brotherhood of Steel.

items.name: Free States01
items.desc: The Free States were a group of Appalachian anarchists who seceded from the United States shortly before the bombs fell.

items.name: Free States02
items.desc: Paranoid that the government was lying to its people about the Vault program, the Free States movement built their own concrete bunkers to survive in case of nuclear devastation.

items.name: Free States03
items.desc: While Raleigh Clay was the public face of the Free States, his arrest would reveal US Senator Sam Blackwell to also be a driving force behind the movement.

items.name: Free States04
items.desc: Most of Appalachia considered the Free States movement to be nothing but political agitators and traitors. After the war, many of these same people would turn to the Free States for help.

items.name: Raiders01
items.desc: The Raider groups of Appalachia were bloodthirsty psychopaths who terrorized the other survivors, taking whatever they wanted from them.

items.name: Raiders02
items.desc: Expert scavengers, the Raider groups of Appalachia were surprisingly ingenious when it came to salvaging old world technology.

items.name: Raiders03
items.desc: After the bombs fell, several wealthy tourists on Appalachian ski holidays reverted to their baser instincts. Selfishness turned to violence, and these entitled elitists became vicious Raiders.

items.name: Responders01
items.desc: After the Great War, Appalachia's emergency personnel mobilized to help their fellow citizens. These Responders became part government, part crisis relief.

items.name: Responders02
items.desc: The Responders provided automated survival training to anyone in need. And it was needed quite a bit.

items.name: Responders03
items.desc: Survival and security became paramount after the devastation of the Great War, and the Responders desperately tried to help as many of their neighbors as they could.
To survive in post-war Appalachia, it's important to make sure you're always stocked with food and water. Keep your thirst and hunger meters filled for extra bonuses.
Objectives and quest targets with a star icon next to them are being shared by your team leader. You are helping them complete this objective and will receive bonus rewards when they do.
Each Shelter has its own workshop budget. Items you build in one Shelter will not count against your C.A.M.P. budget or your budget in other Shelters.
Items with a double-diamond icon next to them are quest items for one of your teammates. Your teammate must pick up this item themselves, so let them know where it is!
Be careful taking too many chems. Not only do you risk addiction, but many chems increase hunger and thirst.
Unlike some other instanced interiors, Shelters are not private. Every player on your server can enter your Shelter, whether they are on your team or not.
Teammates helping you on a quest can fight enemies and locate quest items, but they cannot pick up your quest items or activate terminal entries meant for your quest.
You can craft remedies for diseases at a Cooking Station or Chemistry Station. Without a remedy, a disease will run its course and go away after enough time has passed.
You can use the Shelters Control Panel near the entrance of any Shelter to enter workshop mode. It can also be used to scrap or repair all items in that Shelter.
Natural water sources are irradiated and carry disease. Drink directly from rivers and streams at your peril. When in doubt, boil it out!
Some workshop rules have been relaxed in Shelters. Items won't require support, and can be placed floating!
Raw meat and plant ingredients may satisfy hunger, but cooking them will increase their effectiveness and removes the risk of disease.
The floors in your Shelter act as foundations. You can build directly on them without building foundations of your own.
Diseases spread by being attacked by creatures, eating raw food, swimming in or drinking dirty water, or spending too much time in a hazardous environment.
You can toggle workshop snapping on and off in Shelters at any time using the workshop menu.
Basic cooking recipes will unlock when you first pick up a new type of raw food.
Not all C.A.M.P. items are buildable in Shelters. Some categories and individual items are currently unavailable.
Wearing a Gas Mask or Hazmat Suit will eliminate the risk of Disease from sources like smoke inhalation and being submerged in water.

items.name: Area Targets
items.desc: A circle-shaped quest target on your compass points to a defined area. You can see the size of this area on your map, and once you're inside it, the compass will flash.

items.name: Armor Workbench
items.desc: Use an Armor Workbench to craft your own armor, create modifications, make repairs, or scrap old armor for parts.

items.name: Block Player
items.desc: The "Block For This Session" option will mute the selected Player, block all invites, and hide your location on their map until you log off.

items.name: Bobblehead
items.desc: Using a collected Vault Boy bobblehead will grant a significant, long-term (though temporary) bonus, like an increase to a SPECIAL attribute.

items.name: Boss
items.desc: A crown icon indicates that an enemy is a Boss for this location. Bosses are generally tougher and drop more loot.

items.name: CAMP
items.desc: Use your Construction and Assembly Mobile Platform, or C.A.M.P., to build things critical to your survival, like a Cooking Station, Stash Box, and Weapons Workbench. Place and relocate the C.A.M.P. from the Pip-Boy.

items.name: Chemistry Station
items.desc: The Chemistry Station allows you to craft useful chems and medicines.

items.name: Chems
items.desc: Chems provide temporary bonuses and penalties. You can only be under the influence of one Chem at a time, and using them carries the risk of Addiction.

items.name: Clothing
items.desc: Clothing can be worn over any armor pieces you have equipped. Travel Appalachia in style!

items.name: Containers
items.desc: Any player can access resource Collectors in a C.A.M.P. or public workshop. To prevent theft, build a lock for the Collector, or move the collected items into your private Stash Box.

items.name: Cooking Station
items.desc: The Cooking Station allows you to craft food and beverages that are free of disease and more effective at quenching Hunger and Thirst.

items.name: Crime
items.desc: Repeated unprovoked attacks against other players can cause you to become Wanted, allowing anyone to freely attack you.

items.name: Enemy Blood Eagles01
items.desc: The Blood Eagles revel in violence and bloodshed, and generally attack on sight, with little regard for their own safety.

items.name: Enemy Blood Eagles02
items.desc: Thanks to their anarchic nature, would-be leaders among the Blood Eagles tend to have very limited lifespans.

items.name: Enemy Blood Eagles03
items.desc: The Raiders who reside in the settlement of Crater may be selfish and violent, but they can at least (occasionally) be reasoned with. The same can not be said of the Blood Eagles...

items.name: Enemy Floater
items.desc: The enigmatic and deadly mutant creatures known as Floaters store noxious gases in their flotation bladders, which allow them to move through the air in search of prey.

items.name: Enemy Mothman Cultists01
items.desc: To the cultists who worship the Mothman, Appalachia is holy ground, and all non-believers must be driven out... or destroyed.

items.name: Enemy Mothman Cultists02
items.desc: The Cult of the Mothman is made up of fanatics who seek the blessings of the enigmatic creature known as the Mothman, which they believe is a divine being.

items.name: Enemy Mothman Cultists03
items.desc: The Mothman cultists seek to become one with the divine light, and they believe the Mothman will guide the worthy to this sacred source of everlasting life.

items.name: Enemy Wendigo Colossus
items.desc: As large as it is grotesque, the towering Wendigo Colossus has multiple heads, each of which can attack its prey independently.

items.name: Fast Travel
items.desc: Fast travel quickly moves you to a previously discovered location, but at the cost of caps.

items.name: Fishing Tips
items.desc: Fishing with Improved and Superb Bait will attract increasingly rare and large fish, but only upgraded fishing rods will stand any hope of landing that lunker.

items.name: Hacking
items.desc: Hacking a terminal requires you to have a number of Hacker perks equipped equal to the skill level of the terminal.

items.name: Health
items.desc: You can restore Health by using a Stimpak or similar medication, eating food, or drinking from a water source.

items.name: Help Menu
items.desc: Go to the main menu and select Help to get detailed explanations on topics such as Crafting, using the C.A.M.P., rules for PvP, and more.

items.name: Instancing01
items.desc: Some interiors in the game are private, meaning only you and your teammates can enter. When you approach a private interior, you'll be given the option to enter your own or your team leader's.

items.name: Instancing02
items.desc: In most cases, quest progress in private interiors is only saved once all the activity in the interior is completed. Make sure to wrap up all your current goals before logging off!

items.name: Instancing03
items.desc: Quest progress inside a private interior is personalized. You won't be able to progress your own quest inside your team leader's space.

items.name: Instancing04
items.desc: Curious what dialogue choices your teammate is making? Approach them and select "Listen" to eavesdrop on their conversations.

items.name: Learning Ingredients
items.desc: Sometimes a craftable version of an item will be unlocked by scrapping it, consuming it, or when you pick it up for the first time.

items.name: Level Up
items.desc: Every time you level up, you can increase a SPECIAL attribute and choose a new Perk. After level 50, you continue to choose new Perks, but no longer gain SPECIAL attribute increases.

items.name: Lockpicking
items.desc: Picking a lock requires you to have a number of Picklock perks equipped equal to the skill level of the lock.

items.name: Logout Location
items.desc: Whenever you log into Fallout 76, you'll be spawned near the last location you visited before you logged out.

items.name: Magazine
items.desc: Using a collected magazine grants a temporary, unique bonus. You can find the same issue multiple times, and each time it's used will either award the bonus, or refresh the timer if it's already active.

items.name: Ore
items.desc: Ore, such as Iron Ore and Gold Ore, can be smelted down at a Chemistry Station in order to turn them into crafting components.

items.name: Photomode Personal Loading Screens
items.desc: Pictures you take in Photomode will sometimes appear as personalized loading screens. Memories!

items.name: Power Armor Level
items.desc: You can always enter a suit of Power Armor by using the Transfer button to remove any armor pieces that are higher than your current level.

items.name: Power Armor Station
items.desc: Use a Power Armor Station to repair and make modifications to your Power Armor.

items.name: PVP
items.desc: Outside of specific PvP events, players do reduced damage to other players until both sides have attacked each other.

items.name: Quest Items
items.desc: Items with a diamond icon next to them are important quest items.

items.name: Quest Targets
items.desc: The Data section of your Pip-Boy lists the quests you are on. From there, you can turn quest targets for individual quests on or off.

items.name: Radio
items.desc: The Pip-Boy can be tuned to different radio stations. They will continue to play when you leave the Pip-Boy until you go back in to switch stations or turn the radio off.

items.name: Recipes
items.desc: Recipes and Plans are consumed when you activate them in your Pip-Boy, and teach you how to craft different kinds of items.

items.name: Reputation Fixer01
items.desc: Get on the bad side of the Raiders at Crater or the Settlers of Foundation? Rumor has it someone at the Wayward might be able to help you out...

items.name: Respawn
items.desc: In the event of your untimely demise, you can respawn at your C.A.M.P., a fast travel location, or outside the entrance of Vault 76.

items.name: Scrapped Objects
items.desc: When you're building at a Workshop or C.A.M.P., you can scrap objects to remove them from the world. Doing so will grant half of the components used to build each object.

items.name: Scrapping Junk
items.desc: Over-encumbered? Scrap all your Junk items at a crafting workbench. You'll still have the same crafting components the Junk items would have given you, at a significantly lower weight.

items.name: Sleep
items.desc: Sleeping in a bed will give you a "Rested" bonus that boosts your earned XP for a limited time.

items.name: STASH
items.desc: Need access to certain items but your C.A.M.P. is too far away? You can actually access your Stash at any train station or Red Rocket in Appalachia.

items.name: Stash Box
items.desc: The safest way to store items and equipment is to place them in your Stash Box, which cannot be accessed by other players.

items.name: Storage
items.desc: Containers you build at your C.A.M.P. all share storage. You're limited in how many items you can store, so make use of crafting, scrapping, and trading if you've hit the limit.

items.name: Stored Objects
items.desc: When you're building at a Workshop or C.A.M.P., you can store objects and build them again for free later. Stored objects continue to count towards your build budget.

items.name: Tag For Search
items.desc: The Tag for Search option in the crafting menu will put a magnifying glass icon next to objects that have the components you need.

items.name: Tinkers Workbench
items.desc: The Tinker's Workbench allows you to craft ammo, grenades, mines, and traps.

items.name: Train Stations
items.desc: Every Train Station scattered throughout Appalachia has at least one vendor and a Stash Box.

items.name: Weapons Workbench
items.desc: Use a Weapons Workbench to modify or repair your weapons, craft new ones, or scrap old weapons for parts.

items.name: AC02 Blackout
items.desc: You didn't think the Showmen would let you stroll away so easily, did you?

items.name: Aquarium
items.desc: The Aquarium of the Atlantic's former glory is somewhat faded, but remains impressive as an underwater home for some of the Showmen's most elaborate entertainments.

items.name: Ash Heap01
items.desc: Smoke and cinders constantly bellow up from the mines in the Ash Heap. Survivors believed this was caused by fires in the tunnels below, raging unceasingly for some unknown reason.

items.name: Ash Heap02
items.desc: In the region survivors dubbed the "Ash Heap," a thick layer of filthy smoke blankets the area, providing cover for friend and foe alike.

items.name: Ash Heap03
items.desc: The mines deep within Appalachia's mountains still hold riches for those brave enough to venture below...

items.name: Ash Heap04
items.desc: Before the war, Mount Blair was a large-scale coal mining site where gigantic digging machines removed entire portions of the mountaintop at once.

items.name: Ash Heap05
items.desc: The Garrahans and Hornwrights were the two major families in charge of Appalachia's mining industry. They owned lavish estates in the mountains overlooking their precious mines.

items.name: Boardwalk
items.desc: The famous Atlantic City Boardwalk remains the heart of the city's seaside entertainments. As the seat of the Showmen's power, casual visitors are advised to be wary when their more lethal games are under way.

items.name: Burning Springs01
items.desc: Radhogs are fiercely territorial and will attack anything that gets too close.

items.name: Burning Springs02
items.desc: Radhogs are frequently found near vegetation such as trees, shrubs, and Prickeye Plants, which they nest around and use as a food source.

items.name: Burning Springs03
items.desc: Killing a Deathclaw Handler will send their Deathclaw into a frenzied rage, attacking anything in the vicinity.

items.name: Burning Springs04
items.desc: Abraxodyne Chemical briefcases can be identified by their logo - a yellow star. These briefcases can be found in various places all over Burning Springs.

items.name: Burning Springs05
items.desc: Initial Grunt Hunts will have a one star challenge rating. Complete more Grunt Hunts to unlock tougher contracts.

items.name: Burning Springs06
items.desc: Only one Head Hunt can be active at a time, so team up with others to take out the outlaws.

items.name: Burning Springs07
items.desc: The Prickeye Plant is a new type of flora, exclusive to Burning Springs.

items.name: Burning Springs08
items.desc: The Prickeye Plant can be used in new recipes, which can be obtained by completing challenges.

items.name: Burning Springs09
items.desc: Burning Springs is plagued by erratic sandstorms that affect visibility.

items.name: Casino Quarter
items.desc: The tarnished heart of America's Playground, the Casino Quarter is firmly under the thumb of the Lombardi Family and home to its crown jewel, the Neapolitan Hotel and Casino.

items.name: City Center
items.desc: Though badly flooded, central Atlantic City remains a home to the bulk of its population, who now favor elevated walkways, pontoon bridges, and life above the ground floor.

items.name: City Hall
items.desc: The center of government authority in Atlantic City, the once-grand City Hall is the nerve center for the Munis and their efforts to keep the city running.

items.name: Community Center
items.desc: Despite its poor repair, the Community Center remains a vital part of daily activity for many of Atlantic City's citizens... when the Overgrown aren't driving everyone out, anyway.

items.name: Cranberry Bog01
items.desc: The colorful red florae of the Cranberry Bog were originally West Virginia's naturally occurring cranberry, pitcher, and sundew plants.

items.name: Cranberry Bog02
items.desc: The survivors of Appalachia avoided the Cranberry Bog more than any other region, and only the most well-equipped dared to travel here.

items.name: Cranberry Bog03
items.desc: Allegheny Asylum was originally built in the mid-1800s as a treatment facility for the mentally ill.

items.name: Cranberry Bog04
items.desc: Watoga was built as a joint effort between the federal government, RobCo, and Atomic Mining Services to build a "city of the future."

items.name: Cranberry Bog05
items.desc: All public services in the city of Watoga were designed to be completely automated, including a full staff of security robots.

items.name: Crater01
items.desc: When the Diehards Raider gang returned to Appalachia, they settled in the area of the crashed space station and named their new home the Crater.

items.name: Crater02
items.desc: Meg leads the Raiders at Crater with a cool head and pragmatic nature, but she won't hesitate to employ violence if she or her people are threatened.

items.name: Crater03
items.desc: Many of the Raiders who dwell at Crater are opportunistic and power-hungry, just waiting for a chance to improve their standing even if it means eliminating a rival.

items.name: Crater04
items.desc: Amid the debris of the crashed space station, the Raiders found sophisticated communications equipment they now use to monitor radio traffic in Appalachia.

items.name: Crater05
items.desc: The Raiders believe that strength is the key to survival, and they view the Settlers of Foundation as weak and ripe for conquest.

items.name: Forest01
items.desc: The region surrounding Vault 76 was known as "the Forest" to the survivors of Appalachia. Still rich in plant and animal life, it is an ideal place to scrounge for food and water.

items.name: Forest02
items.desc: Although relatively untouched by the bombs, the Forest region of Appalachia is still home to the mutated beasts that now roam the countryside. Survivors even reported finding mutated plants with unusual properties...

items.name: Forest03
items.desc: While Morgantown was home to Vault-Tec University and experienced something of a re-vitalization before the war, the townspeople all knew the harsh truth: Vault entrance was not guaranteed.

items.name: Forest04
items.desc: Charleston was the capital of West Virginia and one of the largest cities in the area. Prior to the Great War, it was a hotbed of political dissent and saw countless protests for workers' rights.

items.name: Forest05
items.desc: A small town near the Vault 76 construction site, Flatwoods was home to a local motel, tavern, and church. Vault-Tec projections for the survivability of the residents of this area were not optimistic.

items.name: Foundation01
items.desc: A group of identical Protectrons named Sunny serve as vendors at Foundation. Each competes with the others to establish itself as the real Sunny.

items.name: Foundation02
items.desc: The Settlers at Foundation rely on cooperation and collaboration, but respect the guidance of Paige and Ward, who are the closest the settlement has to leaders.

items.name: Foundation03
items.desc: Foundation was constructed on the site of the Spruce Knob campground, affording the Settlers a commanding view of the nearby hills and valleys.

items.name: Foundation04
items.desc: The Settlers at Foundation traveled from a variety of areas to make a new home in Appalachia, but most come from various parts of Pennsylvania.

items.name: Foundation05
items.desc: The settlement of Foundation represents the first step in the Settlers' plan to reclaim Appalachia, through building, expansion and community.

items.name: Foundry
items.desc: Built to last, some industrial buildings like the Foundry survived the Great War relatively intact. The Fanatics seized this stronghold from the Union and now turn its machinery to the production of chemical weapons.

items.name: Human Condition
items.desc: The Overgrown present a seemingly endless problem for the Munis who guard the people of Atlantic City. Mayor Tim has requested reinforcements to help drive back the latest incursion.

items.name: Industrial
items.desc: As a center of industry, Pittsburgh was heavily targeted for bombing during the Great War. The survivors scrape out a living among the shattered remnants of its former industrial might.

items.name: Kanawha County Cemetery
items.desc: The Mothman cultists have claimed the Kanawha County Cemetery as a place of holy communion. By night, they perform rituals in the hopes of summoning their deity.

items.name: Load Screen
items.desc: Half the fun of Nukashine is that you never know what kind of crazy places it will take you.

items.name: Loadscreen
items.desc: A forgotten remnant of an Enclave project, whatever occurred here slipped into obscurity thanks to the Enclave's post-war conflicts.

items.name: Loadscreen
items.desc: Formerly the ATLAS Observatory, Fort Atlas now serves as the headquarters of the new Brotherhood of Steel in Appalachia.

items.name: Loadscreen
items.desc: The machinery beneath Fort Atlas is a legacy of the long-abandoned research once conducted in this facility. Why it bears little resemblance to the mechanisms of a telescope has remained a mystery.

items.name: Loadscreen
items.desc: This underground structure was originally intended to be someone's budget version of a Vault. Its new life as a supply cache for the Brotherhood of Steel is likely to attract unwanted attention.

items.name: Loadscreen
items.desc: The Orwells were in dire financial straits before the bombs fell. Ironically, this expensive shelter failed to save them in the end.

items.name: Milepost Zero
items.desc: Milepost Zero repurposes an old exit tunnel in Shenandoah National Park. It now serves as a base for a new branch of the Blue Ridge Caravan Company.

items.name: Mire01
items.desc: Known as the "Mire" by the survivors of Appalachia, this swampy region is home to twisting vines, large tree canopies, and tall grass. All easy places for things to hide...

items.name: Mire02
items.desc: Mutated plants known as "Strangler" vines infest the Mire. They seem to attach to living things, notably the large trees in the area.

items.name: Mire03
items.desc: The Dyer Chemical plant originally produced animal feed and other phosphates used for nearby farms.

items.name: Mire04
items.desc: Harpers Ferry was a small town that depended on tourism. This put them at odds with the growing "Free States" movement, whose conspiracy theories put off patriotic visitors.

items.name: Mire05
items.desc: Camp Venture was a survival skills training facility, open to tourists who wanted to learn how to rough it out in the wilderness. Hopefully, those lessons came in handy.

items.name: Neapolitan
items.desc: No expense was spared in maintaining the Neapolitan Hotel and Casino as a decadent reminder of pre-war luxury. Under the Lombardi Family, caps and chems alike flow freely here and keep the dream of Atlantic City alive.

items.name: Pier
items.desc: Located just off the Boardwalk, Showman's Pier houses stage shows, arcades, and other distractions for those with caps to spare. Most are even safe.

items.name: Point Pleasant
items.desc: As the ranks of the Mothman cult have grown, its members have settled in the scenic town of Point Pleasant, claiming it as their new home.

items.name: Quentinos
items.desc: High rollers, lowlifes, and made men rub shoulders at Quentino's, Atlantic City's hottest nightclub, named for the reclusive Don Quentino Lombardi.

items.name: Rob Co Research Facility
items.desc: RobCo, a leading corporation in the design and manufacture of robots (as well as the Pip-Boy), maintained contracts with several other corporations and governments... many of which involved unorthodox experiments.

items.name: Rollins Labor Camp
items.desc: Seeking a foothold in Appalachia, the savage Blood Eagles have established a stronghold at the old Rollins Work Camp.

items.name: Rose Room
items.desc: Hailing from faraway Atlantic City, the Russo family has unexpectedly opened a nightclub in their new home of Appalachia. Whether the locals appreciate the effort to bring some nightlife to the region remains to be seen.

items.name: Sanctum
items.desc: True to its moniker, the old church known as the Sanctum was a haven for the lost souls of the Pitt until the Fanatics came. Now it is a house of pain where the Fanatics break the spirits of their captive workers.

items.name: Savage Divide01
items.desc: The region of Appalachia known to survivors as the "Savage Divide" is a mountainous area whose rocky landscape is difficult to cross and easy to get lost in.

items.name: Savage Divide02
items.desc: Before the Great War, the mountains of Appalachia were home to ski resorts, bed and breakfasts, and cabins available to rent by eager tourists.

items.name: Savage Divide03
items.desc: The Top of the World was originally an enormous ski lift station, complete with shops and restaurants at its peak.

items.name: Savage Divide04
items.desc: Nestled in the mountains is a spiritual retreat center known as the Palace of the Winding Path. Its unique architecture stands in stark contrast to the rest of Appalachia.

items.name: Savage Divide05
items.desc: Government facilities dot the landscape of Appalachia's mountains. Trading rumors of the goings on inside those fenced-in walls was a popular pre-war pastime.

items.name: Skyline Valley01
items.desc: The Dark Hollow community of Shenandoah had remained in the park for centuries, until being displaced by the construction of Stolz's manor.

items.name: Skyline Valley02
items.desc: Skyline Drive, constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the 1930's, offers drivers miles of stunning views.

items.name: Skyline Valley03
items.desc: The Appalachian Mountains, Scottish Highlands, Ouachita, and Little Atlas of Morocco were once part of the same geological mountain range.

items.name: Skyline Valley04
items.desc: The Steel Jacks throughout Skyline Valley are dedicated to the young men in the Civilian Conservation Corps who built much of Shenandoah National Park's infrastructure.

items.name: Skyline Valley05
items.desc: Rapidan Camp, built in 1929, served as the presidential retreat during the presidency of Herbert Hoover.

items.name: Toxic Valley01
items.desc: The region known to survivors as the "Toxic Valley" is covered by industrial white powder and polluted water sources.

items.name: Toxic Valley02
items.desc: The lake and other polluted waters of the Toxic Valley region are home to all manner of mutated, aquatic beasts.

items.name: Toxic Valley03
items.desc: Grafton Steel Mill was the center of economic development for the town of Grafton, and its large, industrial machines remain relatively intact.

items.name: Toxic Valley04
items.desc: The town of Grafton was built on the shores of the Tygart Valley River. It was a hub for shipping prior to the Great War, thanks to having both water and railroad access.

items.name: Toxic Valley05
items.desc: Built to provide power to the Steel Mill, the Grafton Dam is now filled with the polluted waters of the Toxic Valley.

items.name: Trench
items.desc: Toxic runoff from ruined factories and lingering radiation made the collapsed streets of the Trench a serious danger for survivors. Then the Trogs showed up.

items.name: Vertibird
items.desc: The Responders' salvaged vertibird has extended their reach considerably, allowing them to make contact with distant communities. Their pilot Lennox insists the refurbished aircraft is "mostly safe."

items.name: Wayward
items.desc: Located on the outskirts of Flatwoods, the Wayward is a bar and gathering place serving the people who've returned to Appalachia to seek their fortunes.

items.name: Whitespring01
items.desc: Built in 1858, The Whitespring was famous for its southern style and sulphur springs.

items.name: Whitespring02
items.desc: The Whitespring Resort had a long history of business with the federal government, and counted sitting US Presidents among its guests.

items.name: Whitespring03
items.desc: Under great financial strain before the war, The Whitespring was forced to sell much of its surrounding land and replace the resort staff with more cost-effective robots.

items.name: Automation
items.desc: Before the Great War, Appalachian mining companies and other industrial interests pursued automation to a near unprecedented degree, leading to widespread job loss and civil unrest.

items.name: Fallout01
items.desc: On October 23rd, 2077, in what came to be known as the "Great War," the world was engulfed in nuclear fire. In the United States, a fortunate minority escaped to the safety of great underground Vaults.

items.name: Fallout02
items.desc: Durable, easy to carry, and quickly recognizable, the Nuka-Cola bottle cap is one of the most common currencies used by traders in post-war America.

items.name: Fallout03
items.desc: The Vault-Tec Assisted Targeting System, or V.A.T.S., grants the user increased combat precision and tactical awareness.

items.name: Fallout04
items.desc: Despite being a land of incredible technological achievement, war and civil strife came to define much of American life by 2077, when things finally erupted into global nuclear Armageddon.

items.name: Vault Tec University
items.desc: In 2031, Vault-Tec re-branded Morgantown's local college as Vault-Tec University, and some of their top executives and scientists either taught or graduated from there. Go Fighting Wendigos!

items.name: Vault76
items.desc: Vault 76 was built to house the best and brightest of America. Unlike most of Vault-Tec's projects, it was exactly what it appeared: a refuge for the future hope of humanity.

items.name: Astonishingly Awesome
items.desc: Finding an issue of Astonishingly Awesome Tales will temporarily give you a unique bonus, like reduced damage from robots or increased RadAway effectiveness.

items.name: Backwoodsman
items.desc: Finding an issue of Backwoodsman will temporarily give you a unique bonus, like cheaper weapon crafting or increased healing from cooked food.

items.name: Bedtime Stories
items.desc: Finding an issue of Tales from the West Virginia Hills will temporarily give you a unique bonus, like increased damage to a specific type of creature.

items.name: Grognak
items.desc: Finding an issue of Grognak the Barbarian will temporarily give you a unique bonus, like increased melee damage or reduced weight for all melee weapons.

items.name: Guns And Bullets
items.desc: Finding an issue of Guns and Bullets will temporarily give you a unique bonus, like increased critical damage from ballistic weapons or additional components from scrapping weapons.

items.name: Live And Love
items.desc: Finding an issue of Live and Love will temporarily give you a unique bonus, like increased Health or damage dealt when you're on a team.

items.name: Scout Life
items.desc: Finding an issue of Scout's Life will temporarily give you a unique bonus, like reduced damage from insects or increased carry weight.

items.name: Telsa Science
items.desc: Finding an issue of Tesla Science will temporarily give you a unique bonus, like reduced damage from Plasma weapons or increased Radiation Resistance.

items.name: Tumblers Today
items.desc: Finding an issue of Tumblers Today will temporarily give you a unique bonus, like making your Bobby Pins unbreakable or increasing your effective skill when picking locks.

items.name: Unstoppables
items.desc: Finding an issue of The Unstoppables will temporarily give you a unique bonus, like the ability to avoid damage from a specific type of weapon.

items.name: USCovert Ops
items.desc: Finding an installment of the US Covert Ops Training Manual will temporarily give you a unique bonus, like increased damage resistance while sneaking or increased damage to other players.
Too much exposure to radiation can cause you to develop Mutations, which have both positive and negative effects.
Contracted a Mutation but want it gone? You can attempt to cure it by using RadAway.
Taking a Mutation Serum will instantly grant you that Mutation. Serums also suppress the negative effects of that Mutation for a limited period of time.

items.name: Action Boy
items.desc: Always running low on Action Points? Equip the Action Boy or Action Girl Perks, and you'll regenerate Action Points faster.

items.name: Adamantium Skeleton
items.desc: Tired of healing wounded arms and legs? The Adamantium Skeleton Perk will reduce all limb damage received.

items.name: Agility
items.desc: Agility is a measure of your overall finesse and reflexes. It determines your Action Points in V.A.T.S. and your ability to sneak.

items.name: Animal Friend
items.desc: The Animal Friend Perk allows you to aim your gun at animals and attempt to pacify them.

items.name: Anti Epidemic
items.desc: With the Anti-Epidemic Perk, curing a disease also has a chance to cure a disease on nearby teammates.

items.name: Archer
items.desc: The Archer Perk increases the damage you deal with bows and crossbows. This stacks with Expert Archer and Master Archer. Equip all three for maximum damage!

items.name: Armorer
items.desc: Why settle for some "off-the-shelf" piece of armor? Craft your own modifications with the Armorer Perk!

items.name: Awareness
items.desc: Why won't that thing just die? Equip the Awareness Perk, and you'll see a target's damage resistances when you're in V.A.T.S.!

items.name: Barbarian
items.desc: Want to channel your inner Grognak? With the Barbarian Perk, you gain increased damage resistance. The higher your Strength, the greater the resistance.

items.name: Blood Sacrifice
items.desc: The Blood Sacrifice Legendary Perk spends HP instead of AP while using V.A.T.S.

items.name: Bloody Mess
items.desc: Equip the Bloody Mess Perk, and you'll do more damage in combat, and enemies will sometimes explode into a gory paste when they die.

items.name: Born Survivor
items.desc: Keep forgetting to use your Stimpaks? Equip the Born Survivor Perk, and you'll automatically use a Stimpak when your health drops too low.

items.name: Butchers Bounty
items.desc: Equip the Butcher's Bounty Perk for an increased chance to find extra meat when searching animal corpses.

items.name: Can Do
items.desc: Feeling hungry? Equip the Can Do! Perk for an increased chance to find extra canned goods when searching containers.

items.name: Class Freak
items.desc: With the Class Freak Perk, the negative effects of mutations are reduced.

items.name: Commando
items.desc: The Center Masochist Perk increases the damage you deal to your targets torso.

items.name: Commando Expert
items.desc: The Fast Fighter Perk increases your movement speed based on your bonus reload speed.

items.name: Commando Master
items.desc: The Number Cruncher Perk increases your weapons damage the more AP cost it has.

items.name: Concentrated Fire
items.desc: With the Concentrated Fire Perk, every additional attack on the same body part in V.A.T.S. improves both your chance of landing a hit, and the damage dealt when you do.

items.name: EMT
items.desc: Keep your team in the fight! Equip the E.M.T. Perk, and players you revive will also regenerate health for a short period of time.

items.name: Endurance
items.desc: Endurance is a measure of your overall physical fitness. It affects your total Health, Action Point drain from sprinting, and chance to get a Disease.

items.name: Exotic Weapons
items.desc: The Exotic Weapon Perk allows for the creation of more esoteric implements of death, like crossbows, black powder guns, the Syringer, and more.

items.name: Field Surgeon
items.desc: Equip the Field Surgeon Perk, and Stimpaks and RadAway will work much more quickly.

items.name: First Aid
items.desc: Need more from your Stimpaks? Equip the First Aid Perk, and they'll heal more damage.

items.name: Fortune Finder
items.desc: Low on caps? Equip the Fortune Finder Perk, and you'll receive a directional audio cue when a Caps Stash is nearby.

items.name: Friendly Fire
items.desc: Forget "stop, drop and roll." Equip the Friendly Fire Perk, and teammates will regenerate Health whenever you hit them with flame attacks (accidentally or not).

items.name: Gladiator
items.desc: With the Gladiator Perk, one-handed weapons do more damage.

items.name: Good Doggy
items.desc: With the Good Doggy Perk, you gain three times the benefits from eating dog food. Yum!

items.name: Good With Salt
items.desc: Food in your inventory will spoil slower if you have the Good With Salt Perk equipped.

items.name: Hacker
items.desc: The Hacker Perk allows you to hack level 1 terminals. This stacks with Expert Hacker and Master Hacker, allowing you to hack level 3 terminals if you have all three equipped.

items.name: Hard Bargain
items.desc: The Hard Bargain Perk gives you better prices when buying and selling from vendors.

items.name: Heavy Gunner
items.desc: The Heavy Gunner Perk increases the damage you deal with non-explosive heavy guns. This stacks with Expert Heavy Gunner and Master Heavy Gunner, so equip all three for maximum damage!

items.name: Home Defense
items.desc: The Home Defense Perk allows you to craft standard traps and turrets.

items.name: Inspirational
items.desc: The Inspirational Perk will give you a bonus to all earned Experience Points whenever you're on a team.

items.name: Intelligence
items.desc: Intelligence is a measure of your overall mental acuity. It affects the Condition and Durability of crafted items, the amount of material gained from Scrapping, and the difficulty of Hacking.

items.name: Intelligence
items.desc: Charisma is your ability to work with others. It affects which Perks you can share with your team, the rewards from completing Group Quests, and the prices you get when buying from and selling to vendors.

items.name: Iron Fist
items.desc: Equip the Iron Fist Perk, and your unarmed attacks do more damage.

items.name: Iron Stomach
items.desc: No time to cook? Equip the Iron Stomach Perk, and you'll be less likely to catch a disease from eating raw food.

items.name: Ironclad
items.desc: The Ironclad Perk increases the amount of damage and energy resistance you gain for wearing armor.

items.name: Junk Shield
items.desc: Equip the Junk Shield Perk, and the more junk you're carrying, the greater your Damage Resistance bonus.

items.name: Last Laugh
items.desc: The Last Laugh Perk gives you a chance to drop a live grenade from your inventory whenever you go down in combat.

items.name: Lead Belly
items.desc: Equip the Lead Belly Perk to reduce radiation damage from eating and drinking.

items.name: Lifegiver
items.desc: The Lifegiver Perk increases your maximum Health.

items.name: Locksmith
items.desc: Keep prying hands off your stuff! The Locksmith Perk allows you to craft locks for your containers.

items.name: Lone Wanderer
items.desc: Who needs other people? Equip the Lone Wanderer Perk, and you'll take less damage and regenerate Action Points faster when you're not on a team.

items.name: Luck
items.desc: Luck is a measure of your general good fortune. It affects the recharge rate of Critical Hits and the Condition and Durability of items you loot.

items.name: Marathoner
items.desc: Equip the Marathoner Perk, and sprinting will consume less Action Points while you are unarmored.

items.name: Moving Target
items.desc: The Moving Target Perk grants a chance to Evade attacks while sprinting. Can't touch this!

items.name: Mysterious Savior
items.desc: Equip the Mysterious Savior Perk, and an unknown ally will occasionally appear and revive you when you're downed.

items.name: Mysterious Stranger
items.desc: Equip the Mysterious Stranger Perk, and an unknown ally will occasionally appear in V.A.T.S. to lend a hand.

items.name: Natural Resistance
items.desc: The Natural Resistance Perk makes you less likely to catch a disease from the environment.

items.name: Nerd Rage
items.desc: The Nerd Rage Perk increases your combat abilities as you lose HP. Genius. Is. ANGRY!

items.name: Overly Generous
items.desc: Give back! The Overly Generous Perk gives your melee attacks a chance to inflict Radiation Damage. The more Rads you have, the higher the chance.

items.name: Pack Rat
items.desc: The Pack Rat Perk reduces the weight of all junk items you carry.

items.name: Pannapictagraphist
items.desc: The Pannapictagraphist Perk will give you a directional audio cue when a Magazine is nearby.

items.name: Percepti Bobble
items.desc: The Percepti-Bobble Perk will give you a directional audio cue when a Bobblehead is nearby.

items.name: Perception
items.desc: Perception is your sense of environmental awareness. It affects your hit chance in V.A.T.S. and the distance that hostiles will show up on your compass.

items.name: Pharma Farma
items.desc: The Pharma Farma Perk gives you an increased chance of finding more first aid chems when you search a container.

items.name: Philanthropist
items.desc: Hate to eat alone? Equip the Philanthropist Perk, and whenever you eat or drink, your teammates will also satisfy a small amount of thirst and hunger.

items.name: Picklock
items.desc: The Picklock Perk allows you to pick level 1 locks. This stacks with Expert Picklock and Master Picklock, allowing you to pick level 3 locks if you have all three equipped.

items.name: Rad Sponge
items.desc: Equip the Rad Sponge perk, and whenever you take radiation damage, you remove radiation damage from your teammates.

items.name: Rifleman
items.desc: The Down Ranger Perk increases the damage you deal to distant foes.

items.name: Rifleman Expert
items.desc: The Scoped-up Perk increases the range of your scoped weapons.

items.name: Rifleman Master
items.desc: The Smart Shot Perk increases the bonus damage you deal when you hit a weak spot while aiming down a scope. Bullseye!

items.name: Robotics Expert
items.desc: With the Robotics Expert Perk equipped, you can attempt to hack robots in order to pacify them.

items.name: Science
items.desc: The Science Perk increases your energy damage based on your Intelligence. Pew pew!

items.name: Science Expert
items.desc: The Pyro-Technician Perk increases your fire damage based on your Intelligence. Is it hot in here?

items.name: Science Master
items.desc: The Cryologist Perk increases your cryo damage based on your Intelligence. Chilling!

items.name: Scrounger
items.desc: Always low on ammo? Equip the Scrounger Perk, and you'll have an increased chance to find extra ammunition in containers.
