items.name: Shotgunner
items.desc: The Easy Target Perk increases the damage you deal to targets that have been crippled.

items.name: Shotgunner Expert
items.desc: The Love the Spread Perk increases the range of your multi-projectile weapons.

items.name: Shotgunner Master
items.desc: The Shotgun Champ Perk increases the damage you deal to crippled targets based on how many projectiles your weapon fires. The more the merrier!

items.name: Starched Genes
items.desc: Want to lock in your current Mutations? Equip the the Starched Genes Perk, and you'll be less likely to be mutated by radiation and RadAway will remove Mutations less often.

items.name: Strange In Numbers
items.desc: With the Strange In Numbers Perk, the positive effects of mutations are stronger if your teammates are mutated too.

items.name: Strength
items.desc: Strength is a measure of your raw physical power. It affects how much you can carry, and determines the damage of all melee attacks.

items.name: Suppressor
items.desc: The Suppressor Perk reduces the damage of any opponent you hit for a short period of time.

items.name: Team Medic
items.desc: With the Team Medic Perk equipped, using a Stimpak also heals nearby teammates for a smaller amount. This effect is increased if you also have the First Aid and Field Surgeon Perks equipped.

items.name: Tenderizer
items.desc: The Tenderizer Perk increases all damage your opponent receives after you hit them, for a short period of time.

items.name: Travel Agent
items.desc: The Travel Agent Perk allows you to Fast Travel while overencumbered at an increased cost.

items.name: Vaccinated
items.desc: With the Vaccinated Perk equipped, you are less likely to catch a disease from a creature's attack.

items.name: Wasteland Whisperer
items.desc: With the Wasteland Whisperer Perk equipped, you can aim at various Wasteland creatures with your gun and attempt to pacify them.

items.name: V94
items.desc: Vault 94 was home to an intentional community founded on principles of faith, nonviolence, and communal life in harmony with nature.

items.name: V94
items.desc: When Vault 94 reopened, its residents sent out ambassadors to search for survivors and invite them to share in the Vault's bounty.

items.name: V94
items.desc: Vault 94 included agricultural research facilities, an extensive seed bank, and Vault-Tec's greatest innovation, a Garden of Eden Creation Kit.

items.name: V96
items.desc: Vault 96 was home to five brilliant scientists, thousands of cryogenically preserved creatures, and an automated security force to keep them both under control.

items.name: V96
items.desc: With its vast gene banks and cryogenic storage bays, Vault 96 was intended to rebuild entire ecosystems in the aftermath of a nuclear war. Or so its residents were told.

items.name: V96
items.desc: The Vault 96 Mainframe incorporated cutting-edge quantum vacuum tube arrays to model, simulate, and conduct rapid genetic experiments.

items.name: V96 Vault System01
items.desc: Vault Missions have multiple ranks. Practice on Novice, then try the Standard or Expert-Rank Missions for greater challenges and greater rewards.

items.name: V96 Vault System02
items.desc: You can earn the rewards from each rank of each Vault Mission once per day.

items.name: Vault 76 Exit
items.desc: Vault 76 was built to save the best and the brightest in the event of a nuclear holocaust. On Reclamation Day, they would emerge and begin to rebuild America. At least that's when they were supposed to...

items.name: Vault System01
items.desc: Vault Missions have multiple ranks. Practice on Novice, then try the Standard or Expert-Rank Missions for greater challenges and greater rewards.

items.name: Vault System02
items.desc: You can earn the rewards from each rank of each Vault Mission once per day.

items.name: 10mm
items.desc: Easily modified, reliable, and packing decent stopping power, the 10mm Pistol is one of the most trusted sidearms in the Wasteland for a reason.

items.name: Alien Blaster
items.desc: The Alien Blaster is a powerful energy beam weapon that can completely disintegrate enemies.

items.name: Broadsider
items.desc: You might think that you'd never see someone walk the hills of Appalachia with a portable naval cannon, but the existence of the Broadsider would prove you wrong.

items.name: Chainsaw
items.desc: The tools of the past have become the weapons of the present. Chainsaws, fire axes, and even rolling pins serve as the arms for many a Wasteland combatant.

items.name: Deathclaw Gauntlet
items.desc: A terrifyingly simple idea, the Deathclaw Gauntlet is built from the severed arm of its namesake.

items.name: Fatman
items.desc: A hand-held catapult might not sound like an effective infantry weapon, but if that catapult launches miniature nuclear bombs? Now you're talking.

items.name: Flamer
items.desc: The Flamer deals sustained energy damage in a wide area directly in front of it.

items.name: Gamma Gun
items.desc: The Gamma Gun deals Radiation damage, and as such is mainly effective against human opponents.

items.name: Minigun
items.desc: The Minigun will spin up faster and faster as you pull the trigger. Once it reaches maximum velocity, it will start firing.

items.name: Ripper
items.desc: A weaponized chainsaw the size of a large knife, the Ripper can tear into opponents, causing devastating melee damage.

items.name: Super Sledge
items.desc: What's more deadly than being hit by a sledgehammer? Being hit by a sledgehammer that has a rocket strapped to it. Behold the design philosophy of the Super Sledge.

items.name: Syringer
items.desc: An exotic weapon, the Syringer is used to deliver a variety of ingenious and cruel chemicals to an opponent.

items.name: Type Automatic
items.desc: Automatic weapons fire continuously as their trigger is pulled. They include the Submachine Gun, and versions of the Assault Rifle and Combat Rifle.

items.name: Type Black Powder
items.desc: Black Powder weapons were considered relics even before the Great War. Extremely slow to reload, they can still be deadly in the hands of an expert.

items.name: Type Explosive
items.desc: Explosive weapons deal damage in a wide area of effect. They include grenades, mines, the Fat Man, and the Missile Launcher.

items.name: Type Heavy Gun
items.desc: Heavy Guns are generally large, bulky, and exceedingly powerful. They include non-explosive energy and ballistic weapons such as the Flamer, Gatling Laser, and Minigun.

items.name: Type Laser
items.desc: Laser weapons, like the Laser Rifle and Laser Pistol, deal energy damage. They can disintegrate foes, leaving behind piles of ash.

items.name: Type Non Automatic
items.desc: Non-automatic weapons fire one shot with each pull of their trigger. They include the semi-automatic and bolt-action versions of the Assault Rifle, Combat Rifle, and Hunting Rifle.

items.name: Type Pipe
items.desc: Pipe weapons, such as the Pipe Revolver and Pipe Rifle, are crude, low-tech and highly modifiable.

items.name: Type Pistol
items.desc: Pistols are typically smaller than rifles and fire faster, but generally do less damage. They include the 10mm, Pipe Pistol, and Black Powder Pistol.

items.name: Type Plasma
items.desc: Plasma weapons, like the Plasma Rifle and Plasma Pistol, deal energy damage. They can melt enemies, leaving behind a pile of "goo."

items.name: Type Rifle
items.desc: Rifles are generally long, of average size, and require two hands to fire. They include the Assault Rifle, Combat Rifle, Hunting Rifle, Laser Rifle, and Submachine Gun.

items.name: Type Shotgun
items.desc: Shotguns, like the pump-action and double-barreled, do more damage the closer you are to the target.
